language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.
language.lessonRating: How do you feel about this exercise?

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.

Bonjour! That's how we say hello in France. My name is Marguerite and I live in the French countryside. My family has owned this winery for many generations. We grow grapes in the vineyards and use them to make wine to sell at the market.

My family uses many different objects at the winery. Today I'm trying to find out which objects are opaque, translucent, and transparent. My grandpapa told me that you can see through transparent materials because they allow most light to pass through.

Materials that you see through a bit because they allow some light to pass through are called translucent. My grandpapa said you cannot see through opaque objects because they don't allow any light to pass through.
Will you help me find examples of these types of objects?
You'll learn more about opaque, translucent, and transparent objects by helping Marguerite complete all the exercises in this lesson. Click on me any time for help!

exercises.title: How much light will pass through?

dialog.text: I'm in the winery cellar, shining my flashlight on different objects to see how much light passes through them. Light can't pass through opaque objects, some light passes through translucent objects, and most light passes through transparent objects. Can you guess how much light will pass through each object?

I'm trying to find out which objects will create shadows. Transparent objects allow light to pass directly through them, so there are no shadows. Opaque objects block light from passing through them, divert the light, and create shadows. Will you help me decide if each statement is true or false?
